name: Portfolio Management

papers.title: Rank-size analysis of optimal portfolio weights with a reverse-engineering application
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the shape of optimal portfolio weights using rank-size analysis. We consider four portfolio selection models: Global Minimum-Variance (GMV), minimum-CVaR, Risk Parity (RP), and the Most Diversified Portfolio (MDP). For each model, we fit seven rank-size specifications to the sorted portfolio weights generated over rolling windows. To compare the fitted specifications, we combine standard goodness-of-fit measures with Cumulative Second-order $\varepsilon$-Stochastic Dominance, an $\varepsilon$-parameterized generalization of Second-order Stochastic Dominance that quantifies the extent to which the exact dominance conditions are satisfied or violated. Empirically applied to major equity indices, this approach provides a systematic criterion for identifying the optimal functional form across diverse market compositions. Furthermore, we address the inverse problem of identifying the generating model from the observed weight structure. We use the calibrated rank-size parameters as inputs to a Random Forest classifier, evaluated by a blocked cross-validation that accounts for the overlap between estimation windows. The parameters separate minimum-risk from risk-diversification strategies and identify the RP and MDP portfolios, whereas the GMV and minimum-CVaR portfolios are difficult to distinguish. These results indicate that rank-size parameters provide a compact and informative description of portfolio allocation geometries.
